messages:
mika: Quick thought — we still don't have a crisp contract for when the blockcache should present a contiguous KV buffer vs a fragmented/scatter view to the attention kernel. This keeps popping up in rollout bugs when pages get evicted mid-request.

sarah: 100% agree. Current kernel paths assume contiguous KV slices (fast path). If we want to avoid copying on every miss, we need kernel support for scatter-gather or a clear API so the cache can decide to stitch.

tom: Short list of tradeoffs I see:
- kernel changes: more complexity in attention loops but avoids copies and extra mem pressure.
- cache-side stitching: simpler kernel but adds latency on misses and increases transient memory.
- hybrid: allow kernel to accept N fragments; cache tries to keep fragmentation <= N via compaction heuristics.

len: Proposal sketch for an API (pseudo-Rust):
```rust
// blockcache returns a view, not necessarily contiguous
pub struct FragmentedKVView {
  pub fragments: Vec<(u64, Arc<[u8]>)>, // (offset within seq, bytes)
  pub holes: Vec<(u64, u64)>, // ranges that must be rehydrated
  pub contiguous_hint: bool, // true if cheap to copy into contiguous buffer
}

impl BlockCache {
  fn read_kv_range(&self, model: ModelId, start: u64, end: u64) -> Result<FragmentedKVView>;
  fn rehydrate_pages(&self, ranges: &[Range<u64>]) -> Result<()>; // async-friendly
}
```

mika: Nice. The key is the kernel can decide: if fragments.len() <= K then use scatter path, else ask cache to stitch (or block until rehydrate). We should default K=4 in the runtime and tune.

olivia: Need metrics: fragmentation_rate, avg_fragments_per_request, rehydrate_latency, stitch_copy_bytes. Ops need those before we enable the kernel path in prod.

infra-bot: perf/job:kv-fragmentation-microbench started (id: kb-2026-42)

sarah: We ran a microbench this morning: contiguous path median 2.4ms, copying-to-contiguous median 6.8ms (p99 45ms due to GC-like pressure in our test harness), scatter-gather kernel up to 4 fragments median 3.1ms (p99 8.9ms). Copying generally spikes p99.

len: That suggests hybrid approach wins for tail. If kernel supports up to 4 fragments we get close to contiguous median with much better p99 than copying.

tom: Edge cases: attention kernels that rely on single large KV pointer (e.g., fused attention) will be hard to retrofit. We should enumerate which kernels are safe to accept fragmented views and which must be given contiguous memory.

mika: Actionable proposal:
1) Add FragmentedKVView to blockcache API + contiguous_hint flag.
2) Implement scatter-gather code path in attention kernels with a fragment limit K (start K=4).
3) Blockcache: add background compaction to keep hot sequences <= K fragments when possible. Also export compaction/cost metrics.
4) Add explicit rehydrate API for sync/async use by kernels.
5) Add perf and regression tests (unit + long-running perf harness) and telemetry.

olivia: And add a safety-config toggle per model to force contiguous-only paths for models with sensitive latency SLOs.

sarah: SGTM. Also we should add a small fuzz test that injects holes mid-attention to validate fallbacks.

len: I'll draft the API PR for blockcache and a telemetry plan. Would like input from runtime folks on the kernel-side patch before we land.

mika: Thanks — I'll pair with len on the API PR. tom, can you own listing which kernels need contiguous-only guarantees?

tom: Yep — will produce a short compatibility matrix next week.

sarah: tiny nit: make sure rehydrate_pages is cancellable and doesn't block scheduler threads.

mika: Good call. Rehydrate should be async and cooperatively cancellable.

olivia: +1 on metrics & safety toggles. Ops will want gradual rollout flags.

infra-bot: perf/job:kv-fragmentation-microbench finished (id: kb-2026-42) — results uploaded to /perf/kv-frag/2026-42.json

mika: OK let's follow up in the RFC thread with the matrix + API PR links. If no objections I'll turn this into a short RFC follow-up doc and the blockcache PR tomorrow.

sarah: No objections from me. :+1:

len: No objections. I'll open a draft.

tom: SGTM.

olivia: 👍

mika: Closing thread — thanks all.
